messages:
alex: heads-up — customer acme-prod reported quota spikes after a sequence of retries + tool calls. They got billed for prompt tokens twice. anyone seen this pattern?

mira: saw similar in staging last week. suspect we increment quota at both request start and again on tool-call completion. :thinking:

sam: can you paste the relevant logs? especially meter increments and retry ids.

alex: pasted logs:
```
INFO 1912345678 request_id=rid-9abc step=request_start reserved=42
INFO 1912345680 request_id=rid-9abc tool_call started
INFO 1912345682 request_id=rid-9abc meter_increment prompt=12 completion=34
INFO 1912345684 request_id=rid-9abc retry triggered
INFO 1912345685 request_id=rid-9abc meter_increment prompt=12 completion=34
```
seems like completion tokens counted twice on retry.

luis: what's the path? toolcalls spawn their own child requests that use `meter.increment` right? We might be double-counting when parent also reserved.

mira: right. current flow: reserve estimated tokens on start, then on completion we increment actual tokens. If retry happens we reserve again and then increment again. We should mark reservation as consumed on increment and avoid double-reserve/increment.

sam: two thread-safety issues: (1) reservation TTL — if request retries we create new reservation id, current code doesn't link them. (2) tool-call attribution — completions from tool-call should attribute to the lowest-level request only, and parent shouldn't increment.

alex: proposal: change meter to `reserveTokens(request_id, estimate, scope)` returning reservation_id. On actual completion we call `consumeReservation(reservation_id, actual_tokens)`; if a retry creates a new reservation we cancel old reservation (release). Also ensure tool-call child requests always use `inherit_reservation(parent_res_id)` when applicable.

mira: patch sketch:
```
// reserve
res = meter.reserve(req.id, est)
// on completion
meter.consume(res.id, actual.prompt, actual.completion)
// on retry
meter.cancel(res.id)
res = meter.reserve(new_req.id, new_est)
```
This would avoid double increments.

rate-limiter-bot: audit: reservation leak detected for rid-9abc, 24 tokens leaked, user=acme-prod

luis: what about burst controls? If we reserve then release on cancel, burst quota should be reclaimed immediately; current rate limiter uses a leaky-bucket and doesn't support release.

sam: yes need change. Two options: (A) use token-bucket with negative allowance support and explicit release, or (B) keep leaky-bucket but track reservations separately and subtract active reservations from available allowance.

mira: (B) simpler to wire. add `active_reservations` counter per key and treat available = bucket_allowance - active_reservations.

alex: also UX: console should show `reserved` vs `consumed` tokens per request to help debugging. add per-request meter view in console traces.

luis: implementation plan: 1) add reservation API + storage; 2) tie tool-call child requests to parent reservation; 3) change rate limiter to account for active reservations; 4) add console traces. I'll take 1+2. sam take 3. mira take 4. target PRs by EOD Friday? :thumbsup:

mira: thanks. I'll add integration test for retry->cancel->reserve flow. 

alex: appreciate it. tagging infra oncall for visibility @oncall-infra

oncall-infra: noted, keep us posted. audit alert threshold lowered for now.

sam: quick note: don't forget metrics: reservation_acquire, reservation_consume, reservation_release, reservation_leak_count.

alex: ok. I'll create follow-up thread with a small design doc.
